deep_dive.title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference
deep_dive.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) achieve superior problem-solving through extended Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation, but the resulting key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with sequence length and creates severe memory bottlenecks, often exceeding GPU capacity for long reasoning traces. Existing KV cache compression methods rely on recent queries to estimate future token importance, implicitly assuming these serve as reliable proxies for future attention patterns. We demonstrate that this assumption fails in long-horizon reasoning: certain decoding steps generate Thought Revisiting Tokens (TRT) that re-attend to distant previous context, such as task-solving plans formulated early in the trace. Through systematic analysis, we discover that queries corresponding to the TRT cluster into a small number of similarity groups in the embedding space. Based on this insight, we propose BeaconKV, a training-free KV cache compression method that maintains beacon queries, compact representatives for each global query cluster, to anticipate which KV pairs will be revisited without storing the entire query history. Across four open-source LRMs and diverse reasoning benchmarks, BeaconKV generally outperforms existing compression methods, achieving up to $5.8\times$ memory reduction while nearly preserving full cache accuracy and improving throughput by over $4.3\times$.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: BeaconKV shows Thought Revisiting Tokens break recent-query importance assumptions in long-horizon reasoning and presents beacon-query-guided KV compression for Large Reasoning Models, relieving cache growth and memory bottlenecks during long CoT inference.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 大型推理模型通过更长思维链提升解题能力，但KV缓存随序列长度线性增长，在GPU显存上形成严重瓶颈。作者发现长程推理中会出现重新关注早期计划的思维重访令牌，使近期查询可作为未来重要性代理的假设失效。BeaconKV提出以Beacon查询引导的KV缓存压缩，针对这类重访行为调节保留策略。该方法可有效压缩KV缓存并保持推理质量，为长思维链部署提供了更可靠的缓存方案。

quick_skim.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
quick_skim.abstract: Prefix caching, in which a serving engine reuses the key and value tensors of a shared prompt prefix across requests, is enabled by default in the major open-source stacks and treated as a transparent optimization. We measure what it costs in reproducibility, and find that the cost rises sharply with weight quantization. Holding the model, decoding parameters, seed, and request order fixed, and issuing every request serially at batch size one, we ran an eighty-episode multi-turn agentic tool-use workload with caching enabled and disabled across two engines and four weight formats. Enabling the cache changed the agent's trajectory on 36.2 percent of episodes at 16-bit precision and on 75.0 percent at four-bit, a gradient that survives re-measurement under a controlled cache configuration. With caching disabled, repeated execution was bit-identical in every configuration, 0 of 800 episodes, which bounds other sources of nondeterminism at 0.5 percent. Repeated cache-enabled runs did diverge, and three experiments locate the cause: a single server-level prompt-cache setting moves run-to-run divergence by 37.5 percentage points, execution order acts only while that setting is active, and restoring cache state makes the cached and recompute paths each reproduce on 40 of 40 items while still differing from each other on 14. Cached serving is deterministic given cache state, and irreproducible in practice because that state is absent from the request and never reset by default. A single-turn bridge shows the divergence reaching task outcomes without shifting aggregate accuracy. We release the harness, logs, and analysis pipeline.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: Empirically studies cache-induced divergence caused by default prefix caching under weight quantization, directly relevant to serving with prefix cache

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Prefix caching reuses shared-prefix KV tensors and is default in major LLM serving stacks. This empirical study shows enabling caching changes agent trajectories in 36.2% episodes at 16-bit and 75.0% at 4-bit quantization, challenging its transparency.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 主流开源LLM服务默认启用前缀缓存，把KV张量复用视为透明优化，但该做法对可复现性的影响此前未被量化。论文固定模型、解码参数、种子与请求顺序，以批大小1在八十轮多轮智能体工具负载上对比两个引擎、四种权重格式开启与关闭缓存的表现。结果显示开启缓存会在16位精度下改变36.2%回合的轨迹，在4位量化下达到75.0%，说明量化显著放大缓存带来的行为分歧。该研究警示前缀缓存并非完全无副作用，服务系统需要透明化并谨慎评估缓存对输出稳定性的影响。

quick_skim.title: Quality Recovery for Quantized KV Caches via Low-Rank Attention Adaptation
quick_skim.abstract: Low-bit key--value (KV) caches reduce the memory required for autoregressive decoding, but the resulting quality loss depends on the model and quantizer. We keep the quantizer fixed and distill the floating-cache model's behavior into low-rank Q/K/V projection updates while the student executes a physically packed incremental cache. Across three seeds, 4-bit affine-cache adapters recover $54.24\%\pm2.47\%$ of the held-out perplexity gap on TinyLlama-1.1B and $75.96\%\pm4.04\%$ on Gemma-4-12B. On the same frozen NF4 Llama-3.1-8B base, one validation-selected run per quantizer recovers $60.42\%$ under KIVI K2V2 and $37.61\%$ under KVarN K4V2, while preserving 180-case associative retrieval. Gemma's score on an official 4K/8K RULER subset rises from 42.80 with the unadapted 4-bit cache to 48.33 after adaptation (46.15 floating), with substantial task heterogeneity. Finally, a 2-bit rank--token sweep reduces TinyLlama's 2-bit PPL from 576.10 to $11.4000\pm0.0059$ across three seeds, versus 10.3988 floating, but restores only 11--12 of 180 retrieval cases. These results show that low-rank projection adaptation can recover held-out quality across fixed cache formats, while perplexity recovery need not restore long-context retrieval.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: KV cache quantization and low-rank adaptation for memory-efficient long-context inference

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Quantized KV caches cut memory but hurt quality. This work freezes the quantizer and distills a floating-cache model into low-rank Q/K/V updates, recovering 54-76% of the perplexity gap on TinyLlama/Gemma while retaining associative retrieval and RULER long-context scores.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 低比特KV缓存可降低自回归解码的内存开销，但会引入质量损失。作者保持量化器固定，将浮点缓存模型的行为蒸馏到低秩Q/K/V投影更新中，让学生在物理打包增量缓存上恢复质量。实验显示4比特仿射适配器在TinyLlama-1.1B上恢复54%困惑度差距，在Gemma-4-12B上恢复76%。该方法为量化KV缓存的长上下文推理提供了一种轻量级质量补偿手段。
